affected_interfaces: vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py::BalanceScheduler.schedule() -> NewRequestData.from_request() call sites (the default Ascend scheduler; both use_v2_model_runner and non-v2 branches)
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: This commit makes NewRequestData.from_request() (vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py) internally call the new vllm/multimodal/utils.py::strip_covered_mm_data(), which sets data=None on every mm feature whose placeholder span is fully inside a prefix-cache-covered region, EXCEPT that when uses_mrope=True it retains the keep_on_cpu metadata fields (e.g. image_grid_thw/video_grid_thw). The upstream Scheduler passes uses_mrope=self.model_uses_mrope (= vllm_config.model_config.uses_mrope). vllm-ascend replaces schedule() with its own copies of the upstream code in 4 schedulers (patch_balance_schedule.py, recompute_scheduler.py, dyntra_lb_scheduler.py, scheduler_profiling_chunk.py), and all of them call NewRequestData.from_request(req, block_ids[, req._all_token_ids]) WITHOUT the new uses_mrope arg, so it defaults to False. Under these schedulers an M-RoPE multimodal model (Qwen2.5-VL/Qwen3-VL/Kimi-VL etc., all supported on Ascend) with a prefix-cache hit covering an mm item will get mm_features[].data=None on the worker; the worker's RopeState.init_prefill_positions() -> model.get_mrope_input_positions() -> iter_mm_grid_thw() (vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_5_vl.py:1261) dereferences mm_feature.data['image_grid_thw'] and crashes. Required adaptation: in each of the 4 schedulers, mirror the upstream change — set self.model_uses_mrope = vllm_config.model_config.uses_mrope (or read vllm_config directly) and pass uses_mrope=self.model_uses_mrope to every NewRequestData.from_request() call (both the use_v2_model_runner branch that passes req._all_token_ids and the plain branch). No worker/model_runner change is strictly needed because worker code (EncoderRunner.prepare_mm_inputs skips data=None items; gather_mm_embeddings uses cached encoder_outputs by identifier) already tolerates stripped data. Validate with an M-RoPE VL model under each scheduler with prefix caching enabled so that mm items fall inside the computed prefix, plus a non-M-RoPE multimodal regression run.
deep_analysis.risk: If not adapted, the default BalanceScheduler (and the Recompute/DyntraLB/ProfilingChunk schedulers) will crash at prefill for M-RoPE multimodal models whenever a prefix-cache hit covers an mm placeholder (TypeError/AttributeError on mm_feature.data in iter_mm_grid_thw), turning a performance optimization into a correctness regression. Non-M-RoPE models are unaffected (data=None is correctly skipped by the worker), so the failure is easy to miss in general multimodal tests and only surfaces with M-RoPE + prefix cache. Additional risk: silently dropping keep_on_cpu fields would produce wrong M-RoPE positions, so the uses_mrope flag must be threaded through all branches, not just the V2 runner branch.

deep_analysis.adaptation_guide:
Commit b09bd69b5bf1 is an NVIDIA-focused change (route DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5.2 DSA models to the CUDA non-compiled breakable-cudagraph path), but its speculative-config and MTP-architecture changes leak into every platform, including Ascend. The genuinely affected surface is MTP spec decoding for DSA models on NPU:

1) DSA MTP draft architecture change (vllm/config/speculative.py: hf_config_override): for model_type in ('deepseek_v32', 'glm_moe_dsa'), the MTP draft hf_config architecture is now rewritten to 'DeepseekV32MTPModel' (previously 'DeepSeekMTPModel'). vllm-ascend only registers 'DeepSeekMTPModel' -> vllm_ascend.models.deepseek_mtp:AscendDeepSeekMTP (which adds conditional ROT-weight support). 'DeepseekV32MTPModel' is NOT registered, so on Ascend it resolves to the upstream generic vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_mtp.DeepSeekMTP (via vllm/models/deepseek_v32/__init__.py's non-CUDA branch), silently losing the ROT-weight handling that AscendDeepSeekMTP provides (vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_mtp.py lines 15-49). Fix: register 'DeepseekV32MTPModel' -> vllm_ascend.models.deepseek_mtp:AscendDeepSeekMTP in vllm_ascend/models/__init__.py register_model() (and confirm DeepSeek V3.2/GLM-5.2 MTP checkpoints still load rot weights correctly).

2) model_returns_tuple mismatch (vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py upstream now returns True for {'DeepSeekMTPModel','DeepseekV32MTPModel','KimiK3MTPModel'}): vllm-ascend overrides this in vllm_ascend/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py (lines 1532-1541) and checks only "'DeepSeekMTPModel' in architectures". With a 'DeepseekV32MTPModel' draft it returns False, but the deepseek_mtp-family forward still returns (logit_hidden, recycle_hidden), so the MTP draft/decode path (used at lines 1101 and 1312 of that file, plus step3p5.py) will mis-handle the tuple and fail. Fix: add 'DeepseekV32MTPModel' to the architecture set in AscendSpecDecodeBaseProposer.model_returns_tuple.

3) Removal of the deepseek_v32 MTP enforce_eager workaround (vllm/config/speculative.py __post_init__): DeepSeek V3.2 MTP no longer forces eager on any platform, including Ascend; verify that ACL-graph capture of the DeepseekV32MTP draft model on NPU is correct (the old FIXME was CUDA-specific, but this changes the default graph mode for v32 MTP on Ascend and needs an e2e check).

Explicitly NOT needing adaptation (neutralized by existing vllm-ascend patches): (a) DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES now includes DeepseekV32ForCausalLM/GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM, but vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_use_v2_model_runner.py overrides VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner to read only VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER (default False), so the MRV2 default does not change Ascend behavior; (b) the new DEFAULT_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH_ARCHITECTURES auto-enable (VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 + CompilationMode.NONE) is neutralized because vllm_ascend/platform.py line 58 force-sets envs.VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH = False, so is_breakable_cudagraph_enabled() returns False on Ascend (same as the existing DeepSeek V4 handling); (c) model-class resolution: DeepseekV32ForCausalLM still maps to the generic deepseek_v2.DeepseekV3ForCausalLM on non-CUDA, and GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM remains overridden by vllm-ascend's registry entry (AscendGlmMoeDsaForCausalLM inherits vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_v2.GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM, which still exists); (d) the fp8-KV-cache relaxation in vllm/models/deepseek_v32/attention.py and common/kernels.py is only on the nvidia/amd code path, which the generic deepseek_v2 path used on Ascend does not execute.
deep_analysis.risk: Medium. After this commit, DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5.2 MTP speculative decoding on Ascend breaks unless adapted: the draft resolves to the generic DeepSeekMTP (bypassing AscendDeepSeekMTP's ROT-weight support) and AscendSpecDecodeBaseProposer.model_returns_tuple returns False for DeepseekV32MTPModel while the deepseek_mtp forward returns a tuple, causing draft-path errors or wrong sampling. The removal of the deepseek_v32 MTP enforce_eager gate also changes the default ACL-graph mode for the v32 MTP draft on NPU and needs e2e verification. The MRV2-default and breakable-cudagraph auto-enable changes are already neutralized by existing vllm-ascend patches (patch_use_v2_model_runner.py and platform.py's envs override), so the blast radius is limited to the MTP spec-decode path plus a default-graph-mode behavior change for v32 MTP.

This commit refactors the CUDA-only Elastic EP reconfiguration pipeline (elastic_execute.py, elastic_state.py, parallel_state._replace_active_groups now returns retired groups instead of destroying them, gpu_worker.py calls elastic_ep_executor.shutdown()). vllm-ascend does not implement Elastic EP (NPUWorker has no elastic_ep_executor), so the elastic_ep/* core changes need NO adaptation. 1. vllm_ascend/distributed/eplb_state.py::AscendEplbState.from_mapping (~line 151): upstream EplbState.from_mapping dropped the num_valid_physical_experts parameter (now internally delegates to the new EplbState.update_mapping). AscendEplbState.from_mapping still declares num_valid_physical_experts and forwards it to super().from_mapping(num_valid_physical_experts=...), which will raise TypeError after upgrade. Fix: remove the param from the signature, stop forwarding it, and re-hook the expert_replica_routing_table refresh by overriding the new update_mapping(model_config, expanded_physical_to_logical) method (call super().update_mapping(...) then refresh_model_routing_tables() for each model_state), since the new flow constructs the mapping via update_mapping rather than via from_mapping's body.

2. vllm_ascend/worker/v2/eplb.py::AscendEPLBController.setup_from_mapping (~line 86): parent EPLBController.setup_from_mapping dropped old_num_physical_experts and GPUModelRunner.setup_eplb_from_mapping (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py, which NPUModelRunnerV2 inherits) now calls self.eplb.setup_from_mapping(model, model_config, mapping) with 3 args. AscendEPLBController's 4-arg override will raise TypeError when invoked. Fix: drop old_num_physical_experts, call AscendEplbState.from_mapping(...) without num_valid_physical_experts (matching new upstream signature).

3. Verify vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_eplb.py: the _wrap_communicator_factory signature guard (group_coordinator/backend/expert_weights/expert_buffer) still passes because create_eplb_communicator's signature is unchanged by the commit; the new EplbState.create_communicator uses model_state.model.expert_weights and model_state.expert_buffer, so confirm these are populated on the Ascend path and that the patched factory (HcclEplbCommunicator) is invoked correctly for torch_nccl backend. NixlEplbCommunicator's removed defer_remote_setup kwarg is not referenced by vllm-ascend.

4. Confirm AscendEplbState.rearrange remains correct with the new rearrange logic (removed num_valid_physical_experts slicing; now uses -1 padding via masked_fill into an extra invalid-index slot). The change is inherited and needs no code change, but validate on NPU.

5. Update the unit test tests/ut/distributed/test_eplb_state.py::test_from_mapping_refreshes_final_mapping to the new from_mapping signature (or exercise update_mapping).
deep_analysis.risk: Low. The breaking signatures (EplbState.from_mapping, EPLBController.setup_from_mapping) are only reachable through the Elastic EP scale-up path, which is CUDA-only and not exercised on Ascend today, so no runtime crash in normal NPU serving. The main risks are (a) a latent TypeError if the inherited setup_eplb_from_mapping path is ever invoked or if upstream starts reusing it outside elastic EP, and (b) silently dropping the expert_replica_routing_table refresh if update_mapping is not overridden in AscendEplbState, which would leave stale routing tables for the dynamic-EPLB/expert-map path on NPU. suggested_test_areas: Ascend 量化配置（AscendFp8Config 等）与 is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible 兼容性
